summary: Describes a way to specify a service in addition to the mobile node identity in Mobile IPv6, for providers offering several services to one subscriber. It is informational.

eli5.summary: One customer may have different plans, like phone and internet. This adds a way to say which one a request is about.

questions: how to choose service in mobile ipv6
how to select service in mipv6
subtitle: A way for mobile devices to specify which service they want when registering with a home agent.

tldr.problem: Mobile IPv6 identifies mobile nodes by address or identifier, but one subscriber may have multiple services (e.g., phone, internet, enterprise VPN) and the home agent needs to know which service is being requested.
tldr.mechanism: A new Service Selection Mobility Option in Mobile IPv6 binding registration messages allows a mobile node to specify a service identifier. The home agent uses this to authorize the requested service, assign appropriate addresses or prefixes, and apply service-specific routing and policies.
tldr.outcome: Mobile service providers can flexibly support multiple services per subscriber, assign service-specific home addresses, apply service-specific quality-of-service, and better manage their networks.

today: RFC 5149 is an Informational specification defining the Service Selection option for both standard Mobile IPv6 and Proxy Mobile IPv6. It has not been obsoleted and remains the primary specification for service selection in Mobile IPv6 deployments.

sections.title: Service Selection in Mobile IPv6
sections.content:
Mobile IPv6 identifies nodes by home address, Network Access Identifier (NAI), or credentials. However, a single mobility subscriber may be provisioned with multiple services—enterprise data access, isolated service domains for business reasons, simultaneous access to different service domains, or different quality-of-service tiers.

Without a way to specify which service is requested, the home agent cannot make the right decisions about address assignment, routing, security policies, or quality-of-service. A mobile customer might want internet access in one location and enterprise access in another.

This RFC defines a Service Selection Mobility Option that allows a mobile node to specify a service during binding registration. The option is optional (old nodes and home agents do not support it) and appears in Binding Update messages before any authorization or authentication options.
sections.eli5: Your phone tells the home agent not just 'I am Alice' but 'I am Alice, and I want the corporate network.' The home agent then knows to give Alice a corporate IP address and apply corporate firewall rules.

sections.title: The Service Selection Option
sections.content:
The Service Selection option is a Mobile IPv6 mobility option with Type 20. It contains a variable-length service identifier string (1 to 255 octets) encoded in UTF-8 and normalized as Unicode NFKC. Valid identifiers include simple names like 'ims' or 'voip', fully qualified names like 'voip.companyxyz.example.com', or domain-specific identifiers.

The identifier MUST be unique among all home agents that the mobile node is authorized to use. A value of zero octets is not allowed. The option appears in Binding Update messages after the Mobile Node-Network Access Identifier (MN-NAI) option if present, and before any authorization or authentication options.

At most one Service Selection option MAY be included in a Binding Update message. The option SHOULD NOT be sent to correspondent nodes because they do not necessarily understand the service selection made between the mobile node and the home agent.
sections.eli5: The option is a text field (like 'voip' or 'enterprise') that the phone includes in its registration message. The home agent reads it and applies the right policies for that service.

sections.title: Processing and Authorization
sections.content:
Mobile node behavior: A mobile node MAY include at most one Service Selection option in a Binding Update message. The option SHOULD only be included in the initial Binding Update sent to a home agent. If the mobile node wishes to change services, it is RECOMMENDED to de-register the existing binding with the home agent first, then register for a different service.

Home agent behavior: Upon receiving a Binding Update with a Service Selection option, the home agent authenticates and authorizes the mobile node, then verifies the node is authorized for the specified service. If not authorized, it returns a Binding Acknowledgement with Status Code SERVICE_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED (151). If service selection changes in a subsequent Binding Update, the home agent re-authorizes and may deny if policies require a different Home Address or Home Network Prefix.

The home agent MAY apply different policies based on the selected service, including Home Address or Home Network Prefix allocation, routing decisions, quality-of-service, and firewall settings. The home agent MAY also affect quality-of-service treatment and traffic policies based on the selected service.
sections.eli5: The phone includes 'enterprise' when registering. The home agent checks if the phone is allowed corporate access, assigns a corporate IP address and policies, and rejects if not authorized. If the phone later wants 'internet', it must unregister first and register again with 'internet'.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The protection of the Service Selection option depends on how sensitive the service information is. If service selection should be kept confidential, Binding Updates and Binding Acknowledgements SHOULD use Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP) in transport mode with a non-null encryption transform to protect message confidentiality. The existing Mobile IPv6 authentication mechanisms protect the option's integrity and authenticity.

The RFC registers the Service Selection option type as 20 and a new Mobile IPv6 Status Code, SERVICE_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED, set to 151. These registrations ensure interoperability and prevent conflicts with other mobility options.
sections.eli5: If the service choice is sensitive, the binding update should be encrypted. The home agent already authenticates the whole message, so the option is protected as part of that.
